class.name: NetwTableHandle
class.brief_description: One replicated table, holding a row per route and a packed array per column.

method.name: commit
method.description: Fixes the written routes and columns as the applied state readers compare against, stamped with the session's own tick. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the wave was applied ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the session this handle names is gone ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the schema is open, a route wave was never written, a column was not written this wave, or a column's element count disagrees with the route count times its declared stride [/codeblock]

method.name: flush
method.description: Saves the committed rows into [param into] as one record of [param database], settling with an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. [param ids] names the row whose route is [code]read_routes()[i][/code]. The caller created the rows, so the caller owns their stable identity. [method NetwDatabase.table_flush] documents the record's shape. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: hydrate
method.description: Loads the saved record from [param into] of [param database], creates fresh routes for its rows, and commits them. Routes are session-scoped, so a hydrate claims new ones rather than restoring the saved ones. Pair them back to the save keys through the settled [Dictionary]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴routes PackedInt64Array freshly claimed, the committed row order ┖╴ids PackedStringArray parallel, the keys the flush wrote [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: of
method.description: The table declared under [param name] in the session governing [param node]. Returns [code]null[/code] and reports when no session governs [param node], or when no schema carries that name. [method Netw.table] is the front door and this is what it returns.

method.name: row_of
method.description: The row holding [param route], or [code]-1[/code] when it is absent.

method.name: rows_of
method.description: The row for each entry in [param routes], preserving input order and returning [code]-1[/code] for each absent route.

method.name: read_births
method.description: The routes added by the latest admitted wave.

method.name: read_column
method.description: The packed values stored in [param column]. A column is addressed by the index its [NetwSchema] declaration returned.

method.name: read_deaths
method.description: The routes removed by the latest admitted wave.

method.name: read_routes
method.description: The routes stored in this table, in row order.

method.name: write_column
method.description: Stages [param data] for [param column]. A column is addressed by the index its [NetwSchema] declaration returned. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the column was staged ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the session this handle names is gone ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the schema is not sealed yet ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA column is out of range, or data's storage type does not match the declared column [/codeblock]

method.name: write_routes
method.description: Stages [param routes] as this table's row identity column. Its size is how many elements every other staged column owes.

members.member: Whether the session this handle names is still alive. A handle outliving its session answers every other member empty and every verb [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST].
Whether this table's frames are sent reliably. Leave it [code]false[/code] for state that the next wave replaces anyway, and set it for a table whose rows a peer cannot afford to miss.
The name this table was declared under, which is the name [method Netw.table] takes.
The session's handle for this table, which is what the flat [code]table_*[/code] verbs on [NetwMultiplayer] take.
The tick carried by the latest committed wave, or [code]-1[/code] before the first commit.
The sealed schema hash this table carries on the wire. Two peers that bound different sets of tables number them differently, and this is what catches that.

signal.name: received
signal.description: Emitted once for each wave this table produced or an arriving frame touched. [param tick] is the one the commit stamped, so several commits inside one tick collapse to the last.
